corinthians1.14.p1.b1.text: Earnestly pursue love and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially the gift of prophecy.

corinthians1.14.p1.b2.text: For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God. Indeed, no one understands him; …

corinthians1.14.p1.b3.text: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, encouragement, and comfort.

corinthians1.14.p1.b4.text: … the one who prophesies edifies the church.

corinthians1.14.p2.b5.text: Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you, unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?

corinthians1.14.p2.b6.text: … such as the flute or harp, how will anyone recognize the tune they are playing unless the notes are distinct?

corinthians1.14.p2.b7.text: Again, if the trumpet sounds a muffled call, who will prepare for battle?

corinthians1.14.p2.b8.text: … You will just be speaking into the air.

corinthians1.14.p3.b9.text: If, then, I do not know the meaning of someone’s language, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and he is a foreigner to me.

corinthians1.14.p3.b10.text: … Since you are eager to have spiritual gifts, strive to excel in gifts that build up the church.

corinthians1.14.p3.b11.text: I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.

corinthians1.14.p4.b12.text: … how can someone who is uninstructed say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?

corinthians1.14.p4.b13.text: I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.

corinthians1.14.p4.b14.text: But in the church, I would rather speak five coherent words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.

corinthians1.14.p5.b16.text: … In regard to evil be infants, but in your thinking be mature.

corinthians1.14.p5.b17.text: “By strange tongues and foreign lips I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to Me, says the Lord.”

corinthians1.14.p5.b18.text: … Prophecy, however, is for believers, not for unbelievers.

corinthians1.14.p6.b19.text: … everyone speaks in tongues, and some who are uninstructed or some unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your minds?

corinthians1.14.p6.b20.text: But if an unbeliever or uninstructed person comes in while everyone is prophesying, he will be convicted and called to account by all,

corinthians1.14.p6.b21.text: and the secrets of his heart will be made known. So he will fall facedown and worship God, proclaiming, …

corinthians1.14.p7.b23.text: … When you come together, everyone has a psalm or a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. All of these must be done to build up the church.

corinthians1.14.p7.b24.text: If anyone speaks in a tongue, two, or at most three, should speak in turn, and someone must interpret.

corinthians1.14.p7.b25.text: Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh carefully what is said.

corinthians1.14.p7.b26.text: And if a revelation comes to someone who is seated, the first speaker should stop.

corinthians1.14.p8.b27.text: For you can all prophesy in turn so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged.

corinthians1.14.p8.b28.text: The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.

corinthians1.14.p8.b29.text: For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace—as in all the churches of the saints.

corinthians1.14.p9.b30.text: Women are to be silent in the churches. They are not permitted to speak, but must be in submission, as the law says.

corinthians1.14.p9.b31.text: If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknowledge that what I am writing you is the Lord’s command.

corinthians1.14.p9.b32.text: So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.

corinthians1.14.p9.b33.text: But everything must be done in a proper and orderly manner.
